question: Irregular verbs regularise at a rate proportional to one over the square root of frequency. How many times faster does a 100-times-rarer verb regularise?
move: When a rule has a square root in it, big gaps shrink fast.
trap: A hundred times, reading the rule as simply proportional.
hint: Only the square root of the frequency gap matters.
steps: Speed of regularising goes as 1 / square root of frequency.
The rarer verb's frequency is 100 times lower.
reference: Lieberman, Michel, Jackson, Tang & Nowak, Quantifying the evolutionary dynamics of language, Nature, 2007
